rows.text: Hm. Pip, stay down. You're leaking like a busted meat bag.
Hm. Moth's burning like a grease fire. Someone grab a bucket.
Hm. That gut wound is festering like bad meat.
Hm. Stop staring at the meat. Let's get the body moved.
Hm. Too much blood in the dirt. Everything's ruined.
Hm. Stop eating raw meat like a starving animal, Moth.
Hm. Stop that noise before I give you something real to cry about.
Hm. Moth, get back here before the frost bites you clean through.
Hm. Grab a rifle, Pip. Don't let them spoil the breakfast.
Hm. This bench feels right. Like a heavy iron skillet.
Hm. Sit down, Pip. Eat your rice before the flies get it.
Hm. It's kibble, not a banquet. Eat it or don't.
Okay so Ash is totally bleeding everywhere, like, we need to help him right now...
Okay so Tuk is totally on fire, like, like, someone get some water right now!
Okay so you look like you're totally burning up, Ash, like really bad...
Okay so Tuk, you should like, come inside because it's totally getting cold out here...
Okay so Ash is like, totally gone, and the grass is just... so much blood...
Okay so Tuk is like, totally losing it with all that raw meat...
Okay so Ash is totally losing it, like, he just smashed the whole table...
Okay so Tuk is totally freezing and he's just walking away without a jacket, like...
Okay so, they're totally coming through the fog with spears and everything, like, oh my god...
Okay so I'm like, totally getting the hang of this bench now...
Okay so eating on the dirt is like totally gross, but at least it's sunny...
Okay so this kibble is like totally gross, but it's better than nothing, I guess...
Moth is down. She is bleeding heavily. Get a medic to her now.
Negative. Stop screaming, Lux. You are making a scene.
We have only two herbal packs left for Moth.
Move the body to the grave. It is getting cold.
Negative. Moth is dead. One casualty in the east field.
Lux is eating raw meat like an animal. We have fourteen meals left.
That table is gone. Moth, sit down and be quiet.
Negative. It is negative four degrees and he has no jacket.
Six hostiles, north wall, emerging from the fog.
The workbench is steady now. Level ten reached.
Eating on the dirt is not efficient.
Eat the kibble or leave it. I do not care.
I think, well, maybe Tuk is going to be okay, but the bleeding looks... it looks bad.
I think, well, maybe he's actually on fire?
I think, well, maybe the infection is spreading, but I don't have much medicine left.
I think, well, maybe... Rook should probably move, or at least, stop just staring at her like that.
I think, well, maybe we should... we should move the body before the crows arrive?
I think, well, maybe he's just stressed, but eating that much raw meat is probably not good.
I think, well, maybe we shouldn't—oh, the table is completely ruined.
I think, well, maybe he shouldn't go out like that without a coat?
I think, well, maybe they're coming from the north, but I'm not... I'm not quite sure.
I think, well, maybe the calibration is finally, actually, settling in correctly.
I think, well, maybe eating out here isn't quite as bad as it looks?
I think, well, maybe this kibble is, um, actually edible?
Lux is leaking too much. Tuk will get the bandage.
Pip, stop rolling in the dirt and get to the water.
Lux smells of rot and sickness.
Pip, stop staring. We need to move her before the rain gets worse.
Lux is dead in the dirt. He was not good meat.
Eat fast, Pip, before the hunger takes you too.
Lux is making too much noise. He acts like a wounded animal.
Pip, the wind will bite your skin. Come back to the warmth.
Tribals in the fog. Tuk will find good meat today.
Tuk makes good things now. The bench is good.
Tuk eats here. The dirt is hard, but the meat is good.
This is bad meat, Pip. Tuk needs real food.
Of course, the violence is quite poorly timed, and my dear Rook is making a dreadful mess of the sandbags.
Of course, the kitchen has decided to stage a pyrotechnic display, and my dear Ash has chosen the dirt to perform his frantic dance.
Of course, my dear Rook, you have managed to turn your own midsection into a petri dish.
Of course, my dear Ash, staring at the deceased will not return her to us.
Of course, the field is now ruined by this unsightly display of mortality.
Of course, my dear Ash, one must assume even the most disciplined among us will eventually succumb to the primal urge to gorge like a starving beast.
Of course, my dear Rook, one must now find a way to play billiards on the floor.
Of course, my dear Ash, walking into a freezing death is a remarkably dramatic way to handle a bad morning.
Of course, the morning fog serves only to hide the unwashed rabble currently attempting to murder us.
Of course you would offer a nod instead of actual praise, my dear Ash.
Naturally, my dear Nate, dining upon the bare earth is a culinary experience I had not anticipated.
Of course, my dear Ash, we are expected to feast upon this gelatinous sludge and dried grain as if it were a banquet.
